text:
toni: Heads-up 1 leads ended up in overflow-pool during the EMEA CSV import window. queue looked fine but routing still fell back. anyone tracking this pattern?

ram: saw the batch. enrichment webhook spiked around 13:05 UTC, a bunch of enrichment calls timed out. fallback policy immediately hands to overflow-pool.

emma: is overflow-pool our hard fallback or is there an intermediate step? historically we used to try a short grace to accept late enrichment.

ram: current flow: claim TTL = 20s, enrichment timeout = 25s, fallback -> overflow. so if enrichment finishes after claim TTL we don't try to reassign.

jordan: that explains it. for CSV imports latency is expected. idea: introduce a "deferred_reassign" fallback that keeps a short grace window (e.g., 40s) where we allow reassign if enrichment returns owner within that window. reduces churn to overflow.

toni: yes please. prefer to avoid permanently changing claim TTL for all traffic. deferred_reassign could be opt-in per route (import vs real-time).

ram: proposing config snippet (canary):

```yaml
routing:
  claim_ttl_ms: 20000
  enrichment_timeout_ms: 25000
  fallback_policy: deferred_reassign
  deferred_reassign_window_ms: 40000
  deferred_reassign_conditions:
    - enrichment.source: hubspot_bulk_import
    - enrichment.confidence: ">=0.6"
```

emma: nice. two quick safety items: 1) gated reassign only if SF last_activity < enrichment.timestamp, 2) cap auto-reassignes per user to avoid email/workflow storms.

jordan: agree. add a reassign_rate_limit_per_user: 3 per hour. also log reassign_attempt and reassign_outcome.

ops-bot: webhook: /enrich returned 1/1 owners (latency 38s) contact 004f9c. event_id=evt_9082

ram: ^ that one is exactly the deferred candidate. enrichment returned after 38s, within proposed 40s window. with deferred_reassign enabled we'd capture it back to the original owner instead of overflow.

toni: ops checklist for canary:
- enable deferred_reassign on imports route (2% of imports)
- instrument metrics: deferred_candidates, reassign_success_rate, overflow_rate_on_imports
- set alert if reassign_failure_rate > 5% or overflow_rate doesn't drop after 6h
- have rollback toggles ready

emma: runbook blurb for support: when a rep says lead missing -> check routing event for claim_acquire/expire, check enrichment latency and enrichment.source, check SF last_activity, check reassign_attempt logs. manual steps: reassign via SF UI if needed.

jordan: i'll draft the PR and include a small migration to add deferred_reassign_window_ms and rate limit defaults. default off.

toni: start canary at 02:15 UTC? monitor for 6h and report back.

ram: PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/lead-routing/pull/897 (WIP)

ops-bot: alert muted for marketing-channel during canary window (02:15-08:15 UTC)

toni: perfect. thanks all  will post summary after the 6h window. :eyes:
